study.question: Does the click-AUC benefit localized to auxiliary product-to-context gradients require their assignment to the correct training examples, and does that dependence interact with the residual-to-context path?
study.hypothesis: Observed: product-only AUC0.6684156159937658 exceeds blocked/click-only0.6678548720585206 by0.0005607439352452; residual-only0.6676246607842132 is lower by0.0002302112743074; both-open0.668457307890924 exceeds product-only by only0.0000416918971582. The R-by-P interaction is0.0002719031714656 in this single-seed factorial. These are controlled local observations, not repeated support or measured gradient conflict. Mechanism hypothesis: product-path auxiliary derivatives encode useful example-specific context information rather than only a shared bias/gradient marginal distribution. Permuting only their destination context rows while preserving forward predictions, labels and private-task derivatives at fixed state should remove a material part of the product-only advantage. Residual transfer may alter this assignment dependence; its direction is not preselected from the positive historical interaction. Earlier whole-aux-label rolling0.6674639465810746 also changed private task learning and cannot by itself locate example alignment in the product context derivative.

study.proposed_difference: Four cells: product_aligned (Roff, Paligned), product_swapped (Roff, Pswap), joint_aligned (Ron, Paligned), joint_swapped (Ron, Pswap). Insert _ProductContextAssignment.apply only at each auxiliary product-context input after existing gates. Forward returns an identical view. For even training B, h=B//2 and a_i=1[history_count_i>0]; eligible_i=a_i AND a_(i+h mod B). Backward in half_swap returns g_(i+h mod B) for eligible rows, g_i otherwise. This is an involutive permutation since eligible_i=eligible_(i+h); empty histories and their occupied partners stay fixed. It preserves each auxiliary matrix and their summed matrix up to row permutation, including global sum and Frobenius norm. Aligned mode returns g unchanged. Both modes compute identical eligibility and execute the same identity wrapper during training; eval bypasses it and accepts arbitrary batch remainders. No saved model state, modules, parameter changes, RNG, label access, hooks on sparse parameter gradients, additional forward scoring passes or file/network operations are added. The shifted cotangent is explicitly a surrogate backward control, not the derivative of the identity forward or a claimed new optimization algorithm. Keep all true labels and four BCEs, unlike the previous label-roll replacement. Review of prior trajectories: every tested single auxiliary source and fav+buy subset under both adapters underperformed the blocked click baseline; cart+fav partially recovered joint performance; fav+buy x1.5 did not rescue it and joint x2/3 lost some gain. These null/negative branches do not establish universal task complementarity, given scale, optimizer and one-seed confounds. No unsuccessful execution or abandoned-branch receipts are supplied; previous_runtime_error is null. Latest knowledge-usage claims are provenance only: prior INFNet/OneTrans/Zenith/MixFormer/EST/SSR consideration does not confirm those mechanisms; the latest path controls support localization only. All new observations and caveats are recorded prospectively here; host should append resulting charged receipts and evidence-linked revisions to scoped memory. Read-only evidence.jsonl is preserved. predictions: At fixed parameter state all four train/eval prediction matrices, true-label losses, Dice updates, click gradients and auxiliary private gradients match their respective historical endpoints; only permitted context cotangents differ.

Primary contrast: delta_off=AUC(product_aligned)-AUC(product_swapped)>0 if correct example assignment matters. Historical product advantage is0.0005607439352452; treat any single-seed difference as preliminary and compare its magnitude, not just sign.
Secondary: delta_on=AUC(joint_aligned)-AUC(joint_swapped); I=delta_on-delta_off tests whether the residual path changes assignment dependence. No directional prediction for I.

Swapped controls keep global product-context gradient sum and squared norm before embedding scatter at fixed state; they may change coalesced per-ID norms and the dense/sparse optimizer trajectory. Log any measured differences without claiming norm-matched total optimization.
No inference capacity or operation difference is expected. Train cost can increase; measured GPU/wall/memory costs, not static expectations, determine efficiency.
falsifiers: If product_swapped retains the aligned advantage over the historical blocked control with substantial swap coverage, the claim that this benefit requires correct example assignment is unsupported at this permutation and seed; consider generic marginal updates or residual batch correlation.

If delta_off is null or negative across later authorized paired seeds, reject the proposed assignment-dependent product mechanism for this setting. One negative implementation result is not a universal mechanism refutation.

If fixed-state forward/private-gradient/click-gradient parity, empty-history zero derivative, or prescribed VJP invariants fail, the experiment is invalid; correct implementation before interpreting performance and retain all costs.
If delta_on-delta_off is unresolved under repetition, residual interaction remains unresolved, regardless of the earlier positive factorial contrast.

A swapped-control loss does not establish gradient conflict, label semantics, production point-in-time validity, global novelty or independence from users. These require separate discriminating evidence.
alternative_explanations: All available results use one host seed and one pass. Fixed-seed replays are implementation bridges, not independent repetitions or estimates of variability.

The swapped rule intentionally substitutes a context cotangent: it is not the ordinary derivative of the unchanged forward BCE. It tests example assignment, not a deployable scalar-objective improvement.

A deterministic half-batch pairing does not establish independence from users, context, targets or time. Repeated users/IDs and correlated context remain; raw user identities are unavailable inside forward.

The row permutation preserves the summed auxiliary product cotangent and Frobenius norm before context embedding scatter, not its alignment with click/residual gradients, per-ID coalesced norms, Adagrad accumulators or later optimization trajectory.
Some occupied examples retain their gradient if their half-batch partner is empty; swapping is confined to occupied pairs. Measure swapped-row fraction before interpreting a weak effect.

Subsequent parameter trajectories and all private task gradients may diverge after context updates, despite fixed-state private-gradient equality. No claim of direct gradient conflict or semantic mediation follows from AUC alone.
Shared-context features can encode broadly useful task biases; benefit may depend on global auxiliary gradient marginals rather than precise row assignment.
Observed negative transfer can arise from ID-dependent sparse optimizer preconditioning or product normalization geometry rather than anti-alignment of task gradients.
The product-only to full difference0.00004169 may be smaller than seed variation. Frozen one-pass dynamics and historical offline label visibility limit transfer claims.
